properties.description:
* WHAT...Nuisance to Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...The Little River basin in central and south-central
Laurens County.

* WHEN...Until 415 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to the
Little River and associated tributaries, as well as other other
poor-drainage areas, including farmland, parks, greenways,
boat-access areas, golf courses, underpasses, and parking lots.
Isolated, shallow flows over roadways is possible.  A few
flood-prone, low-water crossings may become impassible.  A small
culvert washout or two is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 148 AM EDT, Rain has moved out of the advisory area but
storm-total rainfall of 2-5" occurred over the headwaters of
the Little River watershed, causing significant rises along
the Little River and associated tributaries last night. The
Little River has crested and continues to slowly fall. The
Flood Advisory will remain in effect until the Little River
has receded below bankfull levels.

The following streamgauge is above Action/Advisory Stage,
resulting in nuisance flooding along Little River near Little
River Park...

ID: LRLS1
NAME: at Gordon St, in Laurens
CURRENT STAGE: 7.67 feet
ACTION/ADVISORY STAGE: 7.0 feet
MINOR FLOOD STAGE: 10.0 feet
TREND: Falling slowly

ESTIMATED FORECAST: Little River is expected to recede below
Action/Advisory Stage later this morning.

IMPACTS: Between 7.0 and 10.0 feet, expecting nuisance
flooding within Little River Park impacting walking paths and
other low-lying areas. Additional flooding of low-lying areas
near Little River Park is likely including downstream of
Gordon St near E Main St, E Farley Ave, and US 221.
- Some locations that may continue to experience nuisance to
Minor flooding include...Laurens and Mountville.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Stay away or be swept away. River banks and culverts can become
unstable and unsafe.
